skill.name: performance-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze influencer campaign performance by scoring results against targets, ranking platforms and creators, reviewing content quality, and turning metrics into recommendations.
skill.summary: Measures influencer campaign results across platforms, creators, content, engagement quality, and attribution.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer produced many high-severity path traversal and command-pattern hits, but most are Markdown links, templates, metadata, or placeholder labels. The retained risks are the documented YouTube connector command and its API-key dependency, which are legitimate but require installer visibility because they execute local code and read a secret-bearing environment variable.

remediation.suggestion: Make the YouTube connector step opt-in and show the exact command before running it. Document that it should only call the bundled connector script.

remediation.issue: API key access for YouTube metrics
remediation.suggestion: Tell users that YOUTUBE_API_KEY is read only for YouTube analytics and must not be printed, stored, or included in reports.

content.value_statement: Influencer teams often have data spread across platforms, creators, web analytics, and sales systems. This skill turns those inputs into scorecards, rankings, attribution notes, and clear next actions.
actual_capabilities: Scores reach, impressions, engagement, clicks, conversions, and revenue against targets and benchmarks.
Ranks platforms, influencers, and content formats with reasons for top and bottom performance.
Analyzes engagement quality, comment sentiment, and purchase-intent signals from supplied data.
Breaks down conversions by promo code, UTM tracking, direct attribution, and estimated influence.
Produces ranked learnings, renew or drop recommendations, and future campaign guidance.
Can use an optional YouTube connector for measured video metrics when configured.
limitations: Requires campaign data, exports, screenshots, or pasted metrics from the user.
Does not calculate detailed dollar-level ROI; it hands inputs to a separate ROI skill.
YouTube connector use requires local script access and a valid API key.
Statistical winner claims depend on sufficient sample size and benchmark quality.

use_cases.title: Post-campaign performance review
use_cases.description: Turn finished campaign metrics into a scorecard, top performer list, and action plan.

use_cases.title: Creator renewal decisions
use_cases.description: Compare creators by reach, engagement quality, conversions, and strategic fit before renewing contracts.

use_cases.title: Content learning analysis
use_cases.description: Identify which formats, hooks, platforms, and themes should guide the next campaign brief.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze one campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the performance of our [campaign name] influencer campaign. I have reach, engagement, clicks, conversions, and promo code results.

prompt_templates.title: Compare creators
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these influencers from [campaign name]: [handles]. Rank them by reach, engagement quality, conversions, and renewal recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Find winning content patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the campaign content results and identify the best formats, hooks, messages, and platforms. Separate proven winners from ideas that need more testing.

prompt_templates.title: Build a full readout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full performance readout for [campaign]. Use platform exports, web analytics, promo code data, creator reports, targets, and benchmarks. Include attribution limits and next-campaign recommendations.

output_examples.input: Analyze our summer skincare campaign with 10 influencers.
output_examples.output: A campaign scorecard with target comparisons, top three creators, platform performance, conversion notes, and recommended renewals.

output_examples.input: Compare Instagram Reels, TikTok videos, and YouTube Shorts for this launch.
output: Platform ranking by reach and engagement rate.
Format notes that explain why each platform won or lost.
Budget and content recommendations for the next launch.

output_examples.input: Which creators should we keep for the next campaign?
output_examples.output: A creator table with renewal status, evidence, performance risks, and suggested investment level.

best_practices: Provide raw counts, date ranges, targets, and benchmarks whenever possible.
Label data sources clearly as measured, creator supplied, estimated, or benchmarked.
Use the significance rule before treating a creator, format, or platform as a proven winner.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for definitive ROI when cost and revenue inputs are incomplete.
Do not mix campaign periods or platform definitions without noting the mismatch.
Do not treat vanity metrics as success without engagement quality or conversion context.

faq.question: Can this skill analyze campaigns without live platform integrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can work from pasted exports, screenshots, creator reports, analytics numbers, and sales summaries.

faq.question: Does it calculate ROI?
faq.answer: It reports revenue and conversion performance, but detailed ROI math belongs in the separate ROI calculator skill.

faq.question: Can it compare influencers in one campaign?
faq.answer: Yes. It ranks creators by metrics such as reach, engagement rate, conversions, cost efficiency, and renewal potential.

faq.question: Can it analyze comment sentiment?
faq.answer: Yes, when comments or summaries are provided. It separates positive, neutral, negative, and purchase-intent signals.

faq.question: What data should I prepare first?
faq.answer: Prepare campaign dates, creator handles, platform metrics, web analytics, promo codes, targets, and benchmarks.

faq.question: Does the optional YouTube connector need credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The connector requires a YouTube API key and should be used only when the user approves local command execution.
